title: Two Roads Over the Carpathians: The Transfăgărășan and Transalpina Loop from Sibiu

bestPeriod.window: late June to mid-September, when both DN7C and DN67C are certain to be open end to end
bestPeriod.avoid: May and early June (Transfăgărășan still shut above Bâlea Cascadă), and the 15 July-20 August weekend crush at Bâlea Lac

gatewayAirport: Sibiu International (SBZ), 5 km out; Cluj (CLJ) 3 h; Bucharest Otopeni (OTP) 4 h. CFR rail from Brașov 2 h 40.
summary: You climb out of the Făgăraș foothills in second gear, and past the eleventh hairpin the beech forest quits: nothing left but granite, snowmelt and hot brakes. A week of two mountain crossings, one famous, one…
hook: You climb out of the Făgăraș foothills in second gear, and past the eleventh hairpin the beech forest quits: nothing left but granite, snowmelt and hot brakes. A week of two mountain crossings, one famous, one better, stitched together by monasteries, a Vlad Țepeș ruin up 1,480 steps, and valley roads where 60 km takes ninety minutes. For confident drivers who would rather stop twenty times than arrive early.

snapshot.Getting there: Sibiu International (SBZ), 5 km out; Cluj (CLJ) 3 h; Bucharest Otopeni (OTP) 4 h. CFR rail from Brașov 2 h 40.

itinerary.title: Sibiu, and the paperwork that saves the week
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at Sibiu airport, then do the boring things properly: photograph every panel and the tyre tread, confirm the rovinietă is active on the plate, and get the cross-border annex emailed to you. Ask explicitly whether Moldova/Ukraine/Serbia are excluded, they almost certainly are.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk Piața Mare and Piața Mică, cross the Podul Minciunilor, and climb the Turnul Sfatului for the tin-roofed eye-windows that make Sibiu's rooftops famous. The Brukenthal National Museum on Piața Mare holds the best old-master collection in Romania.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Crama Sibiul Vechi on Strada Papiu Ilarian, cellar vaults, ciorbă de burtă, bulz. Then fill the tank at the Petrom on Șoseaua Alba Iulia, because tomorrow's first proper station is 100 km away.

itinerary.title: Foothills, Cistercians and the first ramp
itinerary.morning: DN1 east through Avrig to **Cârța**, where the roofless Cistercian abbey of 1202 sits behind a Saxon fortified church, twenty minutes, and the only Gothic ruin on the route.
itinerary.afternoon: Făgăraș for the moated brick **Cetatea Făgărașului**, then turn south onto DN7C at Cârțișoara. Stop at the Bădea Cârțan museum, then run the easy lower section to **Bâlea Cascadă** (1,234 m). The road narrows and the temperature drops six degrees in fifteen minutes.
itinerary.evening: Sleep at the Bâlea Cascadă chalet by the cable-car station, or drop back to a Cârțișoara guesthouse if beds are gone. Walk the twenty minutes to the waterfall itself before the light goes. Cash only at several kiosks up here.

itinerary.title: The Transfăgărășan, north to south
itinerary.morning: Be at the Bâlea Cascadă barrier by 07:15, the restricted sector opens at 07:00 and the coach traffic arrives around ten. Twelve kilometres of stacked hairpins lift you to **Bâlea Lac, 2,034 m**, a glacial tarn in a rock cirque. Coffee at **Cabana Bâlea Lac** on the shore.
itinerary.afternoon: Through the **884 m Bâlea tunnel**, unlit, wet, single lane each way, headlights on, and out onto the Argeș side, which is the better half: longer sightlines, fewer people, the Piscul Negru switchbacks unwinding for 20 km. Then the **Vidraru dam**, 166 m of concrete arch across the Argeș gorge.
itinerary.evening: **Poenari Citadel**, 1,480 concrete steps up the ridge to Vlad Țepeș's real fortress, roughly 45 minutes up in the cool of the evening. Sleep in Curtea de Argeș.

itinerary.title: Curtea de Argeș to the Parâng gate
itinerary.morning: The Curtea de Argeș Episcopal Cathedral, 1517, with its twisted turrets and the royal tombs of the Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen kings. Breakfast of covrigi from the bakery on Bulevardul Basarabilor.
itinerary.afternoon: DN7 west to Râmnicu Vâlcea, then DN67 along the Subcarpathian shelf through **Horezu**, UNESCO-listed Brâncovenesc monastery and the ceramics workshops on the main road, where the cockerel motif is genuinely local, not imported. Lunch at **Casa Argeşeană** if you leave late enough to still be near Argeș.
itinerary.evening: Arrive **Novaci** at the foot of the Parâng. Refuel here, this is the last reliable pump before Sebeș, 140 km of mountain later. Guesthouse dinner: tochitură and țuică from the plum orchards below town.

itinerary.title: The Transalpina, and Pasul Urdele at 2,145 m
itinerary.morning: Climb DN67C to **Rânca** (1,600 m), a scrappy ski hamlet that exists because of the road. Then keep going: the treeline falls away and the Transalpina turns into the thing people come for, a ribbon on open alpine grass with shepherds' flocks crossing without warning.
itinerary.afternoon: **Pasul Urdele, 2,145 m**, Romania's highest paved pass. Park at the saddle and walk fifteen minutes onto the ridge for the Parâng panorama. Descend past Pasul Ștefanu and Pasul Dengheru to **Obârșia Lotrului**, a road junction with two cabanas and no phone signal.
itinerary.evening: North on DN7A/DN67C down the Sebeș valley, long, narrow, unlit, and slower than the map claims. Sleep in **Sebeș** or push the extra 15 km to **Alba Iulia** for a better dinner.

itinerary.title: Alba Iulia and a rough-road monastery
itinerary.morning: **Cetatea Alba Carolina**, Romania's largest Vauban star fort, seven bastions and the 1918 Union Hall. Walk the Gate III sally-port carvings and the Orthodox Coronation Cathedral.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Râmeț detour**: Teiuș, then a narrowing county road to Râmeț Monastery in its limestone gorge, 45 km and 1 h 15 each way, last kilometres rough but fine in a normal car when dry. (**Cheile Bicazului** is 330 km each way in the Eastern Carpathians: a two-day add-on, not an afternoon.)
itinerary.evening: Back to Alba Iulia. Dinner at Pub 13 inside the bastion walls, then the 20:00 changing of the guard in period Habsburg uniform.

itinerary.title: Saxon fringe and the drop back to Sibiu
itinerary.morning: A10 and A1 south-east, then peel off to **Cisnădioara** for the 12th-century Romanesque church on its conical hill, ten minutes' walk up, the oldest intact church in Transylvania.
itinerary.afternoon: **Cisnădie**'s fortified church tower, then back into Sibiu. Refuel and clean the car before drop-off; Carpathian tar and grit will otherwise appear on the damage sheet.
itinerary.evening: Last dinner at Kulinarium on Piața Mică, then the walls at Strada Cetății. Fly out or take the 06:40 IR to Bucharest.

accommodationStrategy.name: Cabana Bâlea Lac
accommodationStrategy.description: the lake at dawn and dusk without the day-trippers, and your car is already above the 07:00 barrier. Basic, cold, shared bathrooms, cash preferred.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct by phone/Facebook, 4-8 weeks ahead for July-August weekends.

accommodationStrategy.name: Bâlea Cascadă chalet
accommodationStrategy.description: the fallback when the tunnel sector is shut or the lake cabana is full, and the base station for the **Bâlea cable car**, which runs when the road above is closed, the winter way to the **Hotel of Ice**, rebuilt each December from lake ice.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Kronprinz / Casa Luxemburg
accommodationStrategy.description: real parking rather than street roulette, walkable to both squares, and luggage held on your rental-return morning.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3-4 weeks ahead; Sibiu fills for the June Jazz and August Medieval festivals.

logistics.connectivity: Orange and Vodafone cover the valleys; nothing between Piscul Negru and Vidraru, nothing at Obârșia Lotrului. Download offline maps for the whole loop.
logistics.emergency: 112 for everything. Mountain rescue is Salvamont, reachable via 112 or the Salvamont app; the Sibiu and Gorj county teams cover this route.
logistics.weather: Afternoon storms build over Bâlea and Urdele from mid-July; fog can drop the tunnel sector to walking pace in an hour. Snow is possible at 2,000 m in any month.
logistics.bookingWindows: Bâlea Lac and Rânca beds 4-8 weeks for summer weekends; Sibiu 3-4 weeks; the car 6-8 weeks (automatics are scarce and cost 30-40% more).
logistics.money: Romanian leu (RON), roughly 5 RON to €1. Cards work in towns; carry €40, €60 in RON for cabanas, the Poenari kiosk and shepherd cheese stalls.
logistics.transportRules: 50 km/h in towns, 90 on DN roads, 130 on motorway. Zero-tolerance alcohol limit (0.00‰). Dipped headlights compulsory outside towns, day and night. Winter tyres required on snow-covered roads 1 November-31 March.
logistics.permits: Rovinietă mandatory; DN7C's Bâlea Cascadă-Piscul Negru sector is 07:00-21:00 only, with extra restrictions on cyclists and pedestrians in peak weeks. Do not feed the bears on DN7C, it carries a fine and causes the closures.

proTips: Drive the Transfăgărășan **south-bound and early**: barrier at 07:00, Bâlea Lac by 08:15, through the tunnel before the coaches. Northbound afternoon traffic queues 40 minutes at the tunnel on August weekends.
Sleep at Bâlea Lac midweek, not on a Saturday. The same cabana bed costs less and you get the tarn to yourself at 06:00.
Climb Poenari's 1,480 steps at 17:30, not midday, the stairway is shaded and the ridge light on Vidraru is better.
Fill up in Novaci before the Transalpina and in Făgăraș before the Transfăgărășan. There is no fuel between Novaci and Sebeș.
The Transalpina is the better road and almost nobody outside Romania knows it. If weather forces a choice, drive DN67C.
Learn *"Un plin, vă rog"* (fill it up) and *"Se poate cu cardul?"* (can I pay by card?), the second saves you at every cabana till.
If DN7C is shut for weather, take the **Bâlea cable car** from the Cascadă chalet, it runs year-round and gets you to the lake anyway.

raw.Driving legs (km + realistic time): Sibiu→Cârța 40 km/50 min (DN1); Cârța→Făgăraș 25 km/30 min; Făgăraș→Bâlea Cascadă 35 km/55 min; Bâlea Cascadă→Bâlea Lac 13 km/40-55 min (the hairpin ladder); Bâlea Lac→Piscul Negru 20 km/45 min; Piscul Negru→Vidraru 25 km/40 min; Vidraru→Poenari 4 km/10 min; Poenari→Curtea de Argeș 25 km/30 min; Curtea de Argeș→Novaci 155 km/3 h 05 (DN7, then DN67 via Horezu); Novaci→Rânca 18 km/35 min; Rânca→Pasul Urdele 20 km/45 min; Urdele→Obârșia Lotrului 34 km/1 h; Obârșia Lotrului→Sebeș 85 km/1 h 50 (Valea Sebeșului, narrow and pot-holed); Sebeș→Alba Iulia 15 km/20 min; Alba Iulia→Sibiu 70 km/1 h 10 (A10/A1).
raw.Named passes and closure dates: Transfăgărășan DN7C: high point at the Bâlea tunnel, 884 m long, portal at roughly 2,040-2,050 m; **reopened Friday 12 June 2026 at noon** for the season, and the **Bâlea Cascadă (Sibiu) ↔ Piscul Negru (Argeș) sector is open to traffic 07:00-21:00 only**, outside those hours barriers drop. Typical annual closure runs late October/1 November to mid-June; never plan on it before mid-June. Transalpina DN67C: **reopened 29 May 2026** with traffic restrictions; high point **Pasul Urdele, 2,145 m**, the highest road pass in Romania.
raw.Car rental cross-border rules: Take a compact with real torque, not the cheapest 1.0 petrol, you pull 8-12% gradients loaded. The Green Card (Carte Verde) is standard for EU travel, but almost every Romanian rental **restricts or forbids entry to Moldova, Ukraine and Serbia**; going there needs prior **written authorisation** plus an extended Green Card, arranged days ahead and charged (€30, €60). Bulgaria and Hungary are normally permitted with notice. An unauthorised crossing voids CDW entirely.
raw.Vignette: The **rovinietă** is Romania's electronic vignette, mandatory on all national (DN) roads including DN7C and DN67C. Buy at any OMV/Petrom/Rompetrol till, at roviniete.ro or via the eRovinieta app; plates are scanned, no sticker. There is no 7-day product: category A (cars up to 8+1 seats) runs **1 day €3.50 (about 18 RON), 10 days €6 (about 31 RON), 30 days €9.50 (about 50 RON), 60 days €15 (about 79 RON), 12 months €50 (about 263 RON)**, the 2026 tariff, set in euro and billed in lei at the CNAIR monthly rate, so a fortnight's driving costs the price of a coffee stop. A Euro-emissions-banded tariff has been drafted to replace it but was not yet in force at the start of September 2026. Most rentals include it, confirm in writing.
raw.Viewpoints and laybys: Poarta Raiului above Rânca; the Cârțișoara-side terrace on DN7C over the hairpin ladder; the Vidraru dam crest under the Prometheus statue; the Piscul Negru switchbacks; the Urdele saddle car park; the Bâlea Cascadă chalet terrace.
